name: BAM-15

lead: BAM15 is an experimental compound that makes mitochondria burn fuel as heat, and users hope it raises calorie burn and sheds fat for a leaner look. It is traded online as a 'safer DNP'.

It carries protons across the mitochondrial membrane, uncoupling food oxidation from ATP production and raising energy expenditure. In a 2014 screen it was identified as an uncoupler that did not depolarize the plasma membrane, and in mice on a high-fat diet it reduced body fat and improved insulin sensitivity without changing food intake. No human trials have been published.

paras: It is sold as a research chemical, and forum users discuss it as an alternative to DNP during cutting phases. No human routines have been validated.
Human safety is unstudied. Uncouplers as a class can cause overheating, and DNP has been linked to fatal poisonings. BAM15 is not approved.

angle.text: BAM15 is a mitochondrial uncoupler that lets cells burn more calories as heat, which users hope will lower body fat for a leaner look. In mice it reduced body fat on a high-fat diet.

lead: BAM15 is an experimental mitochondrial uncoupler, a small molecule that lets protons leak across the inner mitochondrial membrane so that nutrient oxidation produces heat rather than ATP. It was identified in a 2014 screen as an uncoupler that did not depolarize the plasma membrane.[1]

In mice fed a high-fat diet, oral BAM15 reduced body fat and improved insulin sensitivity without changing food intake in studies reported in 2020.[2][3] Wikipedia notes no human trials.[4] It is discussed in fat-loss communities as a possible alternative to the older uncoupler DNP; no published human data support its use for that purpose.

paras: Uncouplers raise energy expenditure by dissipating the proton gradient used to make ATP.[1] BAM15 was reported to uncouple mitochondria without depolarizing the cell's plasma membrane, a property that distinguishes it from older uncouplers.[1] A 2020 mouse study described it as orally bioavailable.[2]

In diet-induced obese mice, BAM15 decreased fat mass and improved glycemic control.[2][3] It was reported to improve muscle quality in a sarcopenic obesity model,[5] and to reduce mortality and kidney injury in mouse sepsis[6] and inflammation in a mouse endotoxin model.[7] These are animal findings.

Users on looksmaxxing forums discuss BAM15 as a fat-loss compound and compare it with DNP, a uncoupler with documented fatal toxicity. These are anecdotal accounts; no clinical safety data exist for BAM15 in people.
